test_title: RRB NTPC CBT 2 (Level-2) Official Paper (Held On: 16 June 2022 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: A person can acquire Indian citizenship by naturalisation if the person is ordinarily a resident of India for ________ years.
solution:
The correct answer is __**12.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **12 years **implies** the period of 12 months immediately preceding the date of application and for 11 years in the aggregate in the 14 years preceding the twelve months.**
 
• A person shall be deemed to be a Person of Indian origin if he/she, or either of his parents, was born in undivided India or in such other territory which** became part of India after the 15th day of August 1947.**
 
• **Eligibility criteria for application are under the Citizenship Act, 1955 and the Citizenship Rules, 1956.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• **Naturalization** is the legal act or process by which a non-citizen of a country may acquire citizenship or nationality of that country.
 
• **The rules of naturalization vary from country to country **but typically include a promise to obey and uphold that country's laws and taking and subscribing to an oath of allegiance, and may specify other requirements such as a minimum legal residency and adequate knowledge of the national dominant language or culture.
